description: Since 2000 Israel has refused address changes from Gaza to the West Bank even for people who have lived there for many years, and the freeze also ended the family reunification procedure that was the only lawful route.
energy_note: Twenty-six years of the wrong address.

description: In 2011 Israel agreed to let 5,000 West Bank-resident Palestinians with registered Gaza addresses change them. About 2,700 were approved. Against a population in that position numbering many times more.
energy_note: A one-off amnesty, for a fraction.

aspect: The procedure exists and is built to refuse
description: A 'Procedure for handling applications by Gaza Strip residents for settlement in the Judea and Samaria Area' has existed since 2009. A Freedom of Information response revealed it is designed for rejecting applications rather than accepting them. Gisha titled its report on it 'A procedure so special it applies to no one'.
energy_note: A form whose purpose is to be refused.

aspect: The consequence is removal to Gaza
description: Israel has arrested Palestinians whose registered address is Gaza - including people whose home, family and job are in the West Bank - and removed them to Gaza against their will, in some cases where the only suspected wrongdoing was being present.
energy_note: Deported from your own house to a place you've never lived.

aspect: And most of the people it is used against are women
description: Gisha found the procedure is being used to forcibly transfer protected persons within the occupied territory, and that most of the victims are women - typically women who married into the other area.
energy_note: A separation policy that mostly separates wives.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the form she was made to sign
description: Women who had already signed a settlement form when entering Gaza had it used against them to refuse their return to the West Bank. Women who had not signed were pressured into signing as a condition of travelling at all - whether to visit relatives or to return to their own homes.
energy_note: Signing away your address to be allowed through a gate.

aspect: SCENARIO - the impossible choice, as posed at a crossing
description: She is told she may return to the West Bank as her ID says, or sign a form changing her address to Gaza. Her home, husband and job are in Nablus. Her son is in Gaza. The official waits while she decides which of the two to stop seeing.
energy_note: Choose a child or a house. Now, at this window.
notes: Constructed, but this is precisely the bind Gisha documents under the title 'Give up your right to live in the West Bank, or never see your children in Gaza again'.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the 2011 quota, and the arithmetic of it
description: Israel agreed in 2011 to allow 5,000 West Bank-resident Palestinians with registered Gaza addresses to change them; about 2,700 were approved. It was framed as a goodwill measure and functioned as confirmation that the freeze otherwise held.
energy_note: Two thousand seven hundred, out of a problem many times larger.
